note: Who has called this war a state between war and peace, when, in which words, and who they say wants it kept. One entry per dated statement. Quotes are verbatim; a line marked 'via' is a named outlet's rendering; nothing on this page is translated by us. Names of the state: 'neither war nor peace' (Tehran), 'forever war' (the analysts), 'little war' (the White House), 'perpetual war sweet spot' (Dean Street).

entries.name: neither
entries.speaker: Ali Khamenei
entries.role: Supreme Leader of Iran until his death. Speaking to the cabinet five months before the war began.
entries.setting: Cabinet meeting, Tehran, Sunday 7 September 2025. Iran International's English rendering is quoted; the Middle East Forum gives a second one.

lines.text: neither war, nor peace state that the enemy wants to impose on us
lines.via: Iran International, which says he told the cabinet hope and productivity had to prevail over it, part of the enemy's 'psychological war'

lines.text: don't wait for external developments
The Middle East Forum's rendering of the same remark: the 'neither war, nor peace' condition that 'the enemy has imposed on us' was dangerous for the country.
The phrase is older than this war. Tehran has used it for its standoff with Washington for years, and here the Leader names it as something done to Iran, not chosen by it.

entries.wants: The enemy, who he said wants to impose it on Iran.
entries.ends: Self-reliance: hope and work at home, and not waiting for events outside the country.

source.label: Iran International, 29 October 2026, looking back at the 7 September 2025 cabinet address

entries.note: The underlying report is Euronews Persian, 8 September 2025, which we do not translate: https://parsi.euronews.com/2025/09/08/neither-war-nor-peace-khamenei-oil-production-is-low-the-current-atmosphere-is-not-go. The Middle East Forum piece dates the remark 8 September, the Persian report's publication date; the meeting was Sunday the 7th. No English text from the Leader's office could be reached.

entries.name: little
entries.speaker: Donald Trump
entries.role: President of the United States, eleven days into the war.
entries.setting: Touring a pharmaceutical plant in Ohio, asked by Steve Doocy of Fox News whether it was a 'little excursion' or a war.

lines.text: Well, it's both.
It's an excursion that will keep us out of a war, and the war is going to be — I mean for them, it's a war.
The first statement from the American side that the thing is a war for one party and not for the other.

entries.name: neither
entries.speaker: Masoud Pezeshkian
entries.role: President of Iran, at a memorial for the late Supreme Leader.
entries.setting: The third Amin Iran ceremony, Vahdat Hall, Tehran, Wednesday 10 June 2026. Reported by ISNA and IRNA.

lines.text: We must get out of the 'neither war nor peace' policy.
The martyred Leader repeatedly stated that the situation of 'neither war nor peace' must be resolved.
It is impossible to force a country to surrender with aeroplanes and bombing.
Iran is definitely not surrenderable.
We must move forward with dignity in a way that saves the future of our country from crises and storms.

entries.wants: Not said. He presents it as a policy Iran can leave.
entries.ends: Leaving the policy with dignity. Not surrender.

source.label: ANI via NewKerala, from ISNA, 10 June 2026

entries.note: Dawn carried IRNA's account of what reads as the same speech, with the dignity line: https://www.dawn.com/news/2006641

entries.name: forever
entries.speaker: Ali Vaez
entries.role: Director of the Iran project at the International Crisis Group. The day before he had written in The New York Times that this is a forever war in the making.
entries.setting: Interview on Democracy Now, 16 July 2026, after the April ceasefire collapsed and Washington walked away from the memorandum of understanding.

lines.text: what I meant by saying that this is a forever war in the making
there is only one formula that remains, which is the continuation of the conflict in one form or another
we are going to end up in cyclical cycles of violence
there is really no military solution

entries.wants: Nobody by design. He blames divisions inside the Trump administration for wrecking the memorandum.
entries.ends: Both sides go back to the memorandum of understanding and keep its terms.
entries.note: The Times op-ed, 'This Is a Forever War in the Making', 15 July 2026, is behind a paywall and is not quoted here.

entries.name: forever
entries.speaker: Steven Erlanger, asking the question
entries.role: The New York Times, with Vali Nasr of Johns Hopkins, Suzanne Maloney of Brookings, Aaron David Miller of Carnegie and Lawrence Freedman of King's College London.
entries.setting: News analysis, 16 July 2026, headlined 'In Iran, Trump risks another American forever war'. Read in the Philadelphia Inquirer's reprint.

lines.text: the war has created a new, seemingly intractable problem, bottling up the Strait of Hormuz
Both sides looked to the memorandum of understanding as the continuation of the war by other means
Washington's stakes in this war are simply smaller than those for Iran
the days of the Strait of Hormuz fully free for transit are probably over
set objectives that can be achieved, if at all, only through prolonged struggle
lines.via: Lawrence Freedman, on how forever wars start

entries.wants: Iran can wait longer than Washington, Nasr says, because it has more at stake.
entries.ends: A president who decides the cost is not worth it, declares victory and goes home.

source.label: The New York Times via The Philadelphia Inquirer, 16 July 2026

entries.name: forever
entries.speaker: Hamidreza Azizi
entries.role: Senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group.
entries.setting: Essay in Time, 30 July 2026, 'Why Iran Cannot Fight a Forever War'.

lines.text: it is an open-ended campaign: a war of attrition fought over a waterway
Neither Iran nor America has a credible military path to a durable settlement that ends the fighting
it is not clear how it can remain in a permanent state of confrontation with America and the Gulf states
Washington's problem is the diminishing returns on each additional night of bombing

entries.wants: Iran treats the outcome so far as a victory and is trying to fix its terms, but he doubts it can live in the state for long.
entries.ends: The first agreement. Any new one must say who verifies what, in what order, and what happens when a ship is hit.

entries.name: neither
entries.speaker: Masoud Pezeshkian
entries.setting: Press conference in Tehran for National Journalist Day, Saturday 8 August 2026. Reported by Mehr.

lines.text: War cannot continue forever.
Iran seeks to move beyond the current state of 'neither war nor peace', and hopes to do it with dignity and pride for the country.
He said Iran would stand behind whatever the Leader decided on war, and would not accept an agreement imposed through pressure.

entries.ends: Not an agreement imposed by pressure.

entries.name: sweet
entries.speaker: Adam
entries.role: The friend in the thread. The heuristic is named for Dean Street, where it was found.
entries.setting: A text message at 11:58 in the morning, Monday 10 August 2026, two weeks before the site existed. The reply came nineteen minutes later.

lines.text: < 49 = peace
> 55 = war
50 = perpetual war sweet spot
I buy that

entries.wants: Not said. The band names a state the market can live in.

source.label: The thread. The heuristic page carries the rule.

entries.note: The rule became the front page. Every other entry on this page is read against it.

entries.name: little
entries.speaker: Donald Trump
entries.role: President of the United States, six months into the war.
entries.setting: The Oval Office, Monday 31 August 2026, the night two tankers were hit in the strait, asked about a Washington Post report that military leaders worried about a long operation.

lines.text: a relatively small war
lines.via: CBS News, which reported him playing the conflict down in those words

lines.text: The headline that reached Dean Street the next morning read 'relatively little war', and the heuristic that day called it war for a few minutes before the price fell back.

source.label: CBS News live updates, 31 August to 2 September 2026

entries.note: The fuller sentence quoted elsewhere, 'This is a relatively little war for us. This is not a big war', has not been checked against the transcript and is not quoted here.

entries.name: sweet
entries.speaker: Adam
entries.setting: Text messages at 9:49 and 9:50 in the morning, Tuesday 1 September 2026, as strikes pushed the price over the line and back inside it.

lines.text: Point size of WAR could increase with every dollar over 55
Never mind, just perpetual war. Back to work
Damn it feels real when the website says so.
So there were strikes. Before they were reported, markets declared war for a few minutes before retreating.

entries.ends: Not said. The point is that it did not end; the price went back inside the band.

entries.name: sweet
entries.speaker: Kurt
entries.role: Reading Italians reading Deleuze and Guattari reading Clausewitz.
entries.setting: A text message at 9:50 in the morning, Monday 5 October 2026.

lines.text: when capital controls the war machine clausewitzian theory falls apart which is to say there no longer is a discrete goal that can be achieved. No policy end state. Capital always seeks endless profit. There is no end. Perpetual war sweet spot.
It's possible to isolate the Gulf War but after we won the limited war we then spent a dozen years bombing Iraq before the invasion
you can choose your style and flavor but you can't step away from the table

entries.wants: Capital. Profit has no end state, so neither does the war.
entries.ends: Nothing, on this reading. Only the style and flavour change.
entries.note: The only entry on the page that answers the question of who wants it with a name.

entries.name: forever
entries.speaker: Ali Vaez and Mohammad Ayatollahi Tabaar
entries.role: Vaez of the International Crisis Group, whose essay 'The New Forever War: Why America and Iran Fight On Without Victory' leads the November issue of Foreign Affairs. Tabaar of Texas A&M.
entries.setting: Foreign Affairs podcast 'Iran's Long War', recorded 12 October and published 15 October 2026.

lines.text: Nearly eight months since it began, the war in Iran has settled into a grim stalemate.
the continuation of this conflict, despite all of its costs, seems less costly than the alternative
it is a war that we cannot find a solution to, which means that it would continue in one form or another
it's very hard to put a floor under tensions between Iran and the United States
it could become another permanent condition similar to the sanctions
the two sides believe that time is on their side

entries.wants: Both sides, Vaez says: going on costs less than the concessions a deal needs. The magazine's summary of his essay is that Iran prefers deadlock to any compromise on offer.
entries.ends: Some understanding between Iran and its neighbours or between Iran and the United States. Tabaar's version is a small deal for a small deal, step by step; without it he sees only escalation.
entries.note: The essay itself is behind a paywall and is not quoted.

entries.name: neither
entries.speaker: Mojtaba Khamenei, through Mohsen Rezaei
entries.role: Supreme Leader of Iran since his father's death. Rezaei is secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and carried the message.
entries.setting: A meeting between the Leader and Rezaei, Tuesday 27 October 2026, known from the council's readout as Press TV reported it and from Rezaei's own account.

lines.text: Ayatollah Khamenei has placed a premium on the need to secure Iran's conditions for ending the war and the state of 'neither war nor peace.'

He called for efforts to secure the rights and interests of the Iranian people and the Resistance Front through the fulfillment of conditions announced by Iranian officials for ending the war and the 'neither war nor peace' situation.
Rezaei said the Leader had told him it was time to end the state of 'no war, no peace'.
This is the order Pezeshkian cites from here on. No direct words of the Leader on it exist; every line is a readout or someone's account.

entries.ends: The conditions Rezaei set out in September: an end to the war on every front, Lebanon included, and the release of Iran's frozen funds.

source.label: Press TV, 27 October 2026; Iran International, 29 October

entries.note: Rezaei's account: https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610282034. Iran International's analyst Khosro Isfahani notes the readout contains no direct quotation. His own reading of who gains from the state: Tehran keeps its grip on Hormuz, its allies stay in place, and Washington concedes.

entries.name: neither
entries.speaker: Masoud Pezeshkian
entries.role: President of Iran, the day after the Leader's order.
entries.setting: Cabinet meeting, Tehran, Wednesday 28 October 2026. Reported by Mehr.

lines.text: Enemies must not imagine that by increasing pressure and threats, they can weaken the will of the Iranian nation and force the country to surrender
But I still believe we should go [to negotiations] and move beyond the neither-war-nor-peace situation
He pledged to carry out the Leader's wishes and to meet the conditions Iranian officials had set for ending the war.

entries.ends: Negotiations, on the conditions already set.
entries.note: Iran International's account of the factions that week: https://www.iranintl.com/en/202610300238

entries.name: neither
entries.speaker: Kian Sharifi
entries.role: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty, with Radio Farda, the day after the midterm elections.
entries.setting: Analysis, 5 November 2026, 'War, Deal, Or Stalemate? What The Midterms Mean For Trump's Iran War'. Its third scenario is headed 'No War, No Peace'.

lines.text: Whenever I want it to.
lines.via: Trump, asked when the war ends

lines.text: The reason we lost is the war
lines.via: Vice President Vance on X, 4 November

lines.text: Iran may seek to drag it out in the hopes of raising the political and financial costs for Trump
The no war, no peace scenario as he describes it: keep the posture, keep the blockade, keep the escorts through Hormuz, strike when struck. He calls it unstable.

entries.wants: Iran, if a weakened president can be waited out.
entries.ends: Iran's offer: the strait open within two days if its seven conditions are met.

entries.name: neither
entries.speaker: Masoud Pezeshkian
entries.setting: The 72nd anniversary of the state dairy company, Tehran, Monday 9 November 2026. Carried by Press TV, Tasnim and Anadolu from a statement on the presidency's site.

lines.text: The Leader has instructed us to put an end to the current state of neither war nor peace.
We can engage in dialogue with dignity and bring this matter to a dignified conclusion.
Logic dictates that if we can secure our rights through dialogue, we should avoid becoming embroiled in war.
However, we will never surrender in the face of force, intimidation, or bullying.
Two days earlier, at a meeting on fuel rationing, he said the government was working to leave the state with dignity, and that this must not stop planning for fuel and electricity shortages.

entries.wants: Not said. He presents Tehran as ordered out of it.
entries.ends: Talks with dignity. No surrender to force.
entries.note: Anadolu's rendering of the same lines: 'We can negotiate with dignity and resolve the issue with dignity. We favor dialogue and negotiations. However, we will not surrender to force and bullying.' Also on the readings page.
